1) metabolic rate and stress responses to copper differ significantly among local populations of nine-spined sticlebacks and 2) caution has to be taken when using different populations of a single sentinel species in ecotoxicological monitoring.

nine-spined stickelbacks exhibit significant differences in resting metabolic rate, copper-induced stress response and tolerance to copper between local populations, suggesting that caution has to exercised and pilot studies need to be carried out before wild populations of a species are used for environmental monitoring.

the choice of the study species and the population used for ecotoxicology studies has to be carefully thought through.
the physiological responses to stressors can be highly population specific and that this needs to be taken into consideration when using fish as sentinel species in ecotoxicological studies.
